ordinary_premises_and_complete_reasoning.text:
Verdict for premises and primary applications: PASS, conditional on exactly the five authorized whole grants A224, B225, R230, S262 and S272 and all their clarifications. This is an ordinary local worker audit of an unchanged draft, not canonical research acceptance. NEW282 and ROOT276/277/278/281 are data, not additional grants. ROOT283/284/285 and unbound campaigns are excluded. I read all 27 bound mathematical bodies, including both long grant arguments, their ledgers/material changes, the unchanged 744-LF paper, 700-LF parallel argument, ledger, scope and four controlling FINAL notes. The read log records bounded chunks; it does not by itself prove mathematics. Historical duplicate manuscript files are the same bytes. The original statement asks for the complete all-pairs, all-obstacle domain/contact/structural classification; its historical dossier is data. That problem remains OPEN.

The ordinary setting is a finite globally embedded pure rational d-space, d>=1, with specified positive balanced real top cycle, saturated tangent lattices, and an actual positive-growth reference gamma. PA_R consists of continuous functions affine with arbitrary REAL coefficients on a finite RATIONAL spatial complex; it does not mean integral slopes. PA_Z has integral tangent slopes and rational constants. A printed PCC has rational endpoints, finite nonnegative REAL weights summing to one, barycenter at its center, and a center face contained as a face in every endpoint cell on a rational witnessing structure. The envelope is the supremum of ALL printed-PC competitors q<=gamma+u and q<=gamma+O(1), not only continuous or PA competitors. D_R(gamma) is the global uniform closure of genuine relative PA_R PC functions, equivalently the decreasing uniform closure. Local uniform convergence is not its definition.

A224 is retained in its specific balanced fan strict-growth counterexample scope; it is not a general structural converse. B225 supplies the globally embedded compact-support/maximum-principle distinction; compact abstract chart spaces are a different setting. R230 supplies continuous completion of unrestricted competitors, real-endpoint PCC inequalities for their completion, and identification of the continuous-obstacle envelope with |P_gamma(u)-gamma|<=||u||. It does not supply PA approximation. S262 supplies finite raw foundations, the corrected continuity scopes and the noncompact literal obstruction, with its graph results confined to their granted domains. S272 supplies finite actual-reference completion and auxiliaries, actual-reference rational homogeneous jet realization and a finite-PA roof witness with their stated hypotheses. Its completion gives positive finite mixed measures of common mass M=deg(gamma) for ALREADY completed tuples, a proper rational-component height H0>=0, epsilon>0, J0=integral H0 MA(gamma), and integral H0 MA(f_1,...,f_d)<=K_C=(2d/epsilon)CM+J0 whenever every ||f_i-gamma||<=C. Weak convergence against each C_b test and fixed-C weak/BL uniformity are distinct from global uniform continuity. Native210's overall historical evidence verdict stays INCONCLUSIVE. These premises are explicitly assumed, not freshly established by their acceptance flags.

The raw formula is D_f c(tau)=sum_{sigma>tau}c(sigma) f_sigma(n_sigma/tau)-f_tau(sum_{sigma>tau}c(sigma)n_sigma/tau), using inward primitive lifts in the saturated quotient. Tangent-lift changes cancel because the restrictions agree. Signed and zero intermediate cycles are legitimate; positivity is used only for PC factors acting on effective balanced cycles. No factorial is appended to recursion.

I checked whole immediate ORIGINAL statement/proof units in the bound BMPS v1 and BBGS publisher texts, rather than importing an abstract or a ledger flag. BBGS uses a Euclidean quasi-embedding and unit normals with the negative product convention. Embed x as (x,1); tangent metrics are unchanged and its hyperplane requirement is satisfied. If a_sigma is the Euclidean covolume of the saturated lattice and a_v=1, a basis of N_tau plus a primitive quotient lift is a basis of N_sigma. Thus its normal projection is (a_sigma/a_tau)nu_sigma/tau. Replacing lattice weights c by a_sigma c, subtracting an ambient extension of the tangential derivative and using balancing gives B_{-f}(ac)(tau)=a_tau D_f c(tau). This equality applies at EVERY recursion dimension and to signed/zero weights, so it calibrates the actual operator rather than a substitute.

BBGS Proposition 3.12's whole proof distinguishes inherited facets, new facets splitting one affine cell (opposite contributions cancel), and facets of insufficient old dimension (zero). Proposition 3.15 expands two products at codimension two: diagonal terms are symmetric, and the two boundary rays of a wedge pair its cross terms under reflection. Lemma 3.18 tests the conormal sum against every ambient linear form. Proposition 3.19 preserves balancing using that commutation and refinement. Its printed reference to 3.12 at the commutation step must be read as the equality proved in 3.15; no new hypothesis is inserted. Coefficients are real throughout. For PC PA factors, granted all-face supports let one subtract a support at a center; all residual inward slopes are nonnegative. This gives positive raw intersections on effective balanced residuals.

For a balanced one-cycle, bounded PA b,c have primitive-edge IBP. On a bounded edge of primitive length L the contribution is w(b(v)-b(w))(c(w)-c(v))/L, symmetric in b,c. On an unbounded edge bounded affine functions have zero end slope. Degree terms cancel by balancing. Consequently integral b D_c Z=integral c D_b Z. This proves the finite identity used later; the common relative mass follows by replacing bounded differences one factor at a time by gamma, as granted. The positive-functional representation and actual-reference construction underlying the completed operator remain granted foundations, not a new Riesz proof here.

BMPS Definitions 2.18-2.31 and Lemma 2.34 were checked for primitive products/refinement, and Definitions 3.1-3.5 with Lemma 3.4 and Proposition 3.7 for PC/support scope. Lemma 3.4's printed proof inserts an arbitrary center as a rational refinement vertex and expresses endpoint directions using rational primitive multiples; this is not justified for an irrational center and is explicitly NOT imported by NEW282. R230's perspective density and the granted S272 all-face support supply the needed actual passage. Definitions 4.4-4.7, Lemmas 4.6/4.9/4.11 and Proposition 4.8 were checked for finite divisor, symmetry and bounded-IBP conventions; the delegated 2.35 symmetry foundation is replaced here by the complete calibrated BBGS chain. Proposition 3.22/Definition 3.23 concern a specific global regularizable domain, not density of all continuous functions; their compactification/Dini proof is not used. Definition 4.15 fixes positive growth. Definition 6.2, Proposition 6.3, Theorem 6.4, Remark 6.6 and Corollaries 6.7/6.8 fix envelope/contact language; their broad affine/literal/density statements are not premises for NEW282's new proof. BBGS Definition 5.1 uses real endpoints, and Lemma 6.1/Theorem 6.2 therefore do not automatically prove continuity for the printed rational-endpoint class. The example equal to zero on rational points and -1 elsewhere demonstrates the distinction. No AR10-delegated density or analytic Monge--Ampere replacement is used. Recursive foundations inside the five grants and these sources are not all freshly reconstructed; the audit is conditional on the grants.

Ordinary additional tools used are finite-dimensional rational linear algebra, finite cone/face geometry, compactness, nearest-point separation, finite convex combinations and ordinary integration of finite positive measures. Rational cone generation, boundary dual continuity, every needed tree identity, determinant index and limiting-domain antecedent are reconstructed in the following notes. No maximum/cap closure from ROOT276, intrinsic-height improvement from ROOT277, or strictification from ROOT281 is assumed. Only needed ROOT278 claims are proved afresh.

Artifacts: frozen-file-bindings.json records all 77 bound files plus the three manifests and original-task; read-log.jsonl records bounded mathematical/source reads. source-application-audit.json records quote-free URLs, exact versions, hashes, literal LF units, application hypotheses and exclusions. Longer third-party units are confined to LOCALONLY/BMPS-whole-units.txt and LOCALONLY/BBGS-whole-units.txt. Rerun binding verification: python verify_inputs.py. Hash matches and read flags establish provenance or recorded coverage, never mathematical acceptance.

ordinary_premises_and_complete_reasoning.summary: Affine duality, global same-reference rational-geometry REAL PA approximation and finite raw contact pass.
ordinary_premises_and_complete_reasoning.detailedSummary: Continuous printed PC equals ordinary full-plane convexity with legal incidences and rational-face density. Boundary dual continuity, exact rec generators, finite rational primal samples with real heights, closed epigraph generation, global conjugate error, rational projected faces and actual decreasing extraction are reconstructed. Finite unrestricted envelopes and saturated flat-lineality raw zero are checked.
ordinary_premises_and_complete_reasoning.text:
Verdict for the entire affine duality, epigraph approximation, finite-envelope and finite-contact argument: PASS under n1's explicit premises. The reconstruction keeps the actual REAL reference and its exact recession; no irrational maximum wall is silently declared rational, and no PA_Z endpoint is asserted.

First continuous printed PCC convexity on a full rational affine plane is ordinary convexity. The printed rule permits rational witnessing structures, not just one fixed carrier. A rational box containing a segment is a cell in a finite rational decomposition of the whole plane; its common refinement with a carrier is legal. This is a direct witness, not an assumed coarsening of an arbitrary complex. One can alternatively verify the conclusion within a fixed rational complex: restrict to each closed cell, approximate endpoints and their real barycentric combination inside its rational feasible face, and pass the PCC inequality by continuity. For a rational segment its crossings with rational faces have rational parameters. At a crossing, the minimal center face is a face of both incident endpoint cells. The two nearby rational endpoints give a legal PCC there, forbidding a downward convexity kink. Finitely many cell intervals and these crossing inequalities give convexity along that segment. Rational endpoint pairs are dense in the full affine plane; continuity gives all real pairs. For density inside a face, collect the active rational equations, solve in a rational affine basis, approximate its coordinates, and keep the inactive strict inequalities. For a constrained PCC use perspective variables t_i=alpha_i x_i: sum alpha_i=1, sum t_i=center, and A_i t_i<=alpha_i b_i form a rational feasible polyhedron; density in its minimal face preserves positive active alpha_i. Thus no rational-point inequality is applied to an open face without its density argument. Ordinary convexity directly implies every PCC inequality. The unrestricted envelope identification still uses R230, rather than assuming its original competitors continuous.

For a finite continuous convex f on R^d, epi f is closed convex. The nearest epi point to (x,f(x)-t) exists by restricting the distance minimization to a large compact ball. The squared-distance inequality gives an inward unit supporting normal. The distance is at most t, so the nearest points tend to (x,f(x)); a subsequence of normals tends to a unit supporting normal there. Its vertical component is nonnegative since epi f is upward closed. If it were zero, its horizontal part would pair nonnegatively with y-x for EVERY y in R^d, hence would vanish. That contradicts unit length. Dividing by its strictly positive vertical component yields a supporting affine plane. Every supporting plane lies below f and a support touches at each x. Therefore f(x)=sup_p(p.x-f*(p)), f*(p)=sup_x(p.x-f(x)). This proves the duality actually used, without an analytic MA theorem.

Every top-cell affine piece of a finite convex PA gamma is a global support: its interior derivative supports by segment convexity. Finitely many pieces and continuity give gamma=max_i(p_i.x+b_i), with REAL p_i,b_i. Let Delta=conv{p_i}, possibly irrational, and h(v)=max_i p_i.v. Then |gamma-h|<=max_i|b_i|. Positive recession growth means h(v)>0 for v!=0. Compactness of the unit sphere makes it coercive, and separation implies 0 is in the interior of the full-dimensional compact Delta.

The rational carrier's recession cones cover the FULL plane. For any direction v, some cell contains an unbounded subsequence t_k v; divide all that cell's inequalities by t_k to see v in its recession cone. On that cone the corresponding piece's recession slope equals h: translate a point of the cell by t v and use |gamma-h| bounded. Quotient out rational lineality, take a pointed section, and solve finite rational active systems for its vertices; lift their rational ray generators and include both signs of a rational lineality basis. With these finite rational r_j, epi h=cone{(r_j,h(r_j)),(0,1)}. A direction in any rec cone has a nonnegative generator representation and h is linear there, giving one inclusion; convex subadditivity of h gives the reverse. Pairing all generators gives Delta={p:p.r_j<=h(r_j)}: the inequalities imply p.v<=h(v) for all v, and separation from conv{p_i} proves membership. Lifted heights may be irrational; directions and spatial geometry remain rational. These are the exact original recession rays, not perturbed ones.

If ||f-gamma||<=C, then gamma*-C<=f*<=gamma*+C. For p=sum t_i p_i, gamma(x)>=p.x+sum t_i b_i bounds gamma*(p) above, while evaluation at zero bounds it below. A separating direction makes it infinite outside Delta. Hence f* is finite bounded convex lsc on precisely Delta. Continuity at its WHOLE boundary is essential. At any p in Delta, choose a finite generating set v_i for its tangent cone and anchors p+eta v_i in Delta. Every sufficiently nearby y has y-p=sum a_i v_i with a_i>=0 and sum a_i<=A||y-p||. To see the coefficient bound, eliminate linear dependencies from a nonnegative representation until its active columns are independent; inverse bounds over the finitely many independent subsets give a common A. Then y is a convex combination of p and those fixed anchors with non-p weight tending to zero. Convexity gives limsup f*(y)<=f*(p); lsc gives liminf>=f*(p). This proves continuity at each point, hence uniform continuity on the compact possibly irrational polytope. No relative-interior-only theorem is substituted.

Continuity of f permits rational primal samples with REAL heights: f*(p)=sup_{x rational}(p.x-f(x)). At each p choose one rational sample with error less than eta. Continuity of f* and of its affine sample makes that sample valid on a neighborhood in Delta. Compactness supplies finitely many such samples A, and g_A=max_{x in A}(p.x-f(x)) satisfies f*-eta<=g_A<=f* on all Delta. Set E_A=conv{(x,f(x)):x in A}+epi h. A compact hull plus closed cone is closed (subsequence of compact summands), and the projection is all R^d. The support representation with domain Delta gives f(x+v)<=f(x)+h(v), so E_A is inside epi f and its finite lower boundary F_A satisfies F_A>=f. F_A is finite everywhere because any fixed sample plus epi h supplies a finite height at every position. Its conjugate is exactly g_A on Delta: a linear functional (p,-1) has supremum max_A(p.x-f(x)) on the compact summand and zero on the recession cone when p in Delta. Outside Delta that cone gives infinite supremum. Applying the proved support duality to F_A yields f<=F_A<=f+eta GLOBAL, not just on sampled positions or a compact set.

E_A has finitely many faces. Every lower face is the hull of its active lifted samples plus its active lifted rays; projection is the hull of rational positions plus the cone of rational directions. A finite lower graph face projects injectively, and graph-face intersections project to their intersections and faces. The lower boundary therefore has a finite rational spatial complex despite its real heights/slopes. There are no vertical boundary faces over a finite full-domain convex function. Thus F_A is actual PA_R PC with bounded difference from the SAME gamma before any completed operator is used. For errors e_n=2^-n, choose f<=F_n<=f+e_n and set G_n=F_n+4e_n. Then G_n-G_{n+1}>=4e_n-5e_{n+1}=3e_n/2>0; the weaker bound e_n-e_{n+1} stated in FINAL also holds. ||G_n-f||<=5e_n. This is an actual decreasing global-uniform extraction.

For a bounded finite real-PA obstacle u, pointedly refine its common rational carrier with gamma. Each piece of a=gamma+u is affine on a rational polyhedron with finitely many rational base vertices/rays. Bounded u has zero recession slope on each ray, so its epigraph piece is generated by REAL vertex heights, (r,h(r)), and (0,1). The closed convex hull of the union of all pieces equals the compact hull of all lifted vertices plus the cone of all listed rays. The nontrivial inclusion uses closure: mixing a hull point with weight 1/t at a piece point tending along t r adds r in the limit. Repeat for finitely many rays and scale. The other inclusion contains each whole piece, and the compact-plus-cone set is closed. It lies above convex gamma-||u|| and has full projection, so its lower boundary F is finite. Every continuous convex minorant g of a contains the closed hull in epi g, hence g<=F; also F<=a. By R230 and the proved PC/convex equivalence, F is the PRINTED unrestricted envelope. Its projected graph faces are rational by the same active-generator argument, and a constant sequence places it genuinely in D_R(gamma).

At a noncontact vertex of this finite envelope, the finite support/strict-floor premise from S262/S272 forces a nontrivial flat local PCC relation. For completeness, normalize nonnegative relations among the finite rational star generators. If every relation had positive slope cost, compactness/separation gives an affine floor with strictly positive margin on all generators. Its small upward translate lies below the envelope on an outer collar and below the obstacle in the positive-gap inner ball. The maximum raises the envelope while preserving PC and growth, a contradiction. On a full plane this maximum is ordinary convex; it need not be asserted rational PA. Hence a flat relation exists.

Let g be the convex homogeneous full-plane germ and ell a supporting linear form; b=g-ell is nonnegative subadditive. Flatness and nonnegative weights imply b(d_i)=0 for every active generator. For an active nonzero rational d_j the relation expresses -d_j as a nonnegative combination of the other active directions, so b(-d_j)=0. Both subadditive bounds give b(x+t d_j)=b(x) for every x and real t. The rational linearity fan has a common nonzero rational lineality. Modulo ell all its cells contain that line; recursively its balanced divisor cycles retain it, so after d dimension drops no zero-dimensional cell remains and the raw product is zero. This is on the saturated lattice/quotient, not an unsaturated normal convention. Refinement independence transfers zero to every rational refinement, including artificial cuts. Thus every positive finite raw atom lies on contact, and the finite-envelope raw contact integral is zero. These arguments reconstruct all unnumbered rationality, hull, locality and finite-contact claims in this portion of both unchanged presentations.

ordinary_premises_and_complete_reasoning.summary: Legal finite trees and existing-domain measure limits prove all-C_b affine contact under the stated grants.
ordinary_premises_and_complete_reasoning.detailedSummary: Bellman infima and monotone fixed points equal the actual envelope; near-optimal trees have compact proper-height tails. SAME-reference DC auxiliaries give supported signed-TV bounds and mixed telescoping for two already completed tuples. Independent endpoint membership and fixed-C moments precede weak/contact limits; compact PA approximation is local only.
ordinary_premises_and_complete_reasoning.text:
Verdict for the reconstructed Bellman trees, localized completed-measure continuity and all-C_b affine passage: PASS under n1 and n2. The domain antecedent of EVERY endpoint is proved before a measure is assigned. Needed ROOT278 conclusions are derived here; its historical status gives no authority.

For any finite-valued F, T F(x) is the infimum of F(x) and sum alpha_i F(x_i) over ALL printed legal finite PCC splits at x, each with its rational incidence witness. Weights may be real. With a=gamma+u, ||u||<=C, define F_0=a and F_{k+1}=T F_k. T is monotone, allows no-op and fixes PC functions. Thus gamma-C<=F_{k+1}<=F_k<=gamma+C. Its finite limit F_infty satisfies T F_infty=F_infty: for each finite split its nonnegative weighted sum commutes with the descending limit, and infimum over split and over k commutes. The no-op is included in that set. Fixed-point equality is exactly all printed PCC inequalities. Every printed PC minorant q of a lies below F_0, and q<=F_k implies q<=T F_k. Hence q<=F_infty. Conversely F_infty is itself a finite PC competitor below a with bounded difference from gamma. It therefore equals the ACTUAL unrestricted envelope. Only now R230 identifies it as continuous real-endpoint PC. No continuity or measure of the iterates was presumed.

Induction identifies F_k with the infimum of costs of finite legal splitting trees of depth at most k. For the upper bound choose a split nearly attaining T and then near-optimal subtrees at its finitely many children; distribute an arbitrary error among their nonzero weights. The lower bound is monotonicity at every node. A no-op leaf terminates a branch. Each node has its own legitimate witnessing rational structure; a global barycenter condition alone is insufficient. A finite tree gives a terminal probability nu and preserves the cost sum of gamma+u. It is not an MA measure and receives no operator normalization.

Let H=gamma+c>=0 be proper. Positive growth makes this possible: the finitely many rec cones cover the support, their unit sections are compact, and the positive recession slopes have a positive minimum; on finite bounded remainder the continuous gamma has a finite lower bound. If the tree is e-optimal at x, its terminal cost is <=P_gamma(u)(x)+e<=gamma(x)+C+e. Since -u<=C, integral H dnu<=H(x)+2C+e. Therefore nu{H>R}<=(H(x)+2C+e)/R. Evaluate the SAME legal tree for another obstacle v with ||v||<=C. On {H<=R} the cost change is at most sup_{H<=R}|u-v|; on the complement it is at most 2C times that tail. Reverse u,v and let e decrease to zero to obtain
|P_gamma(u)(x)-P_gamma(v)(x)|<=sup_{H<=R}|u-v|+2C(H(x)+2C)/R.
The height sublevel is compact. On a compact root set H(x) is bounded, so bounded local-uniform obstacle convergence, including nets, yields local-uniform envelope convergence. This uses finite near-optimal trees and compact-height tails, not an assumed attained infimum or an infinite probabilistic process.

Localized measure continuity concerns TWO ALREADY completed tuples. First take finite genuine PA tuples a,b, a compact rational PA test psi supported in K, and telescope the d mixed factors. Each term has the form integral psi D_{a_i-b_i} Z_i, where Z_i is the positive balanced one-cycle from the other PC factors. Bounded primitive IBP from n1 moves a_i-b_i onto D_psi Z_i. Local raw recursion gives supp D_psi Z_i subset K: outside the support psi is identically zero on a neighborhood, hence all linear parts are zero there, also after refinement. There is no enlargement of support to an arbitrary collar.

The S272 SAME-actual-reference auxiliaries give a genuine DC expression for epsilon eta_psi psi as the difference of two PC relative PA auxiliaries (or their already completed versions after the finite passage). Intersecting each with Z_i gives positive mixed measures of mass M. Consequently the signed measure D_psi Z_i has total variation <=L_psi=2M/(epsilon eta_psi). It follows that
|integral psi [MA(a)-MA(b)]|<=L_psi sum_i sup_K|a_i-b_i|.
This is a finite mixed telescope; nonnegativity is not claimed for D_psi. Signed TV is what bounds it. The auxiliaries must be actual D_R(gamma) elements, not formal slopes or smooth bumps. The five grants provide precisely these auxiliaries.

For two completed tuples choose global uniform genuine PA approximants for EACH tuple and apply the finite estimate before passing to their independently defined completed measures. Their differences converge uniformly on K, so the same estimate holds. If completed tuples with a fixed bound C converge locally uniformly to an independently completed tuple, the estimate and compact PA test density give vague convergence. Here that density is only on compact supports: approximate a continuous compact test on a compact neighborhood and use the common mass M to control the uniform error. It does not assert density of compact PA functions in all C_b globally.

Before taking any weak/contact limit, apply the granted all-tuple moment bound integral H0 MA<=K_C, including to the completed endpoint. It gives MA{H0>T}<=K_C/T. A compact cutoff equal to one on {H0<=T} reduces each C_b test to the vague limit, with the remaining bounded test tails <=2||test|| K_C/T. Thus one obtains convergence against each bounded continuous test. This proves the stated ordinary weak/net continuity on fixed-C families; it neither proves global uniform weak continuity nor admits new endpoints into D_R(gamma).

To pass contact, take bounded continuous u and C=||u||+1. Construct compactly supported rational-affine PA u_n with ||u_n||<=||u||+1/n and u_n->u locally uniformly. An explicit local construction cuts u off continuously on an exhausting compact set, keeps its norm, and approximates its positive and negative parts by finitely many rational norm tents. Choose a rational Lipschitz constant large enough that tents outside a small neighborhood cannot overshoot the target, then a sufficiently fine rational grid and rational heights. Uniform continuity controls the error inside that neighborhood; zero outside the enlarged compact support controls it outside. Finite maxima of these rational tents are PA on rational geometry. Their difference has norm at most the target norm plus the approximation error because both parts are nonnegative. Refining for the two parts gives the claimed u_n. This is a local exhaustion approximation, not global uniform C_b density.

R230 makes f=P_gamma(u) and f_n=P_gamma(u_n) continuous convex relative to gamma. N2 independently puts EVERY one of these endpoints in D_R(gamma) by global decreasing approximation. The finite hull result puts each f_n in actual finite PA and its constant sequence is a second domain check. N2's finite contact gives integral (f_n-gamma-u_n) MA(f_n)=0. The tree estimate proves f_n->f locally uniformly; localized completed-measure continuity gives weak C_b convergence on this fixed C family. The gaps g_n=f_n-gamma-u_n and g=f-gamma-u lie in [-2C,0] and converge locally uniformly. On a compact cutoff their varying integrals converge by local convergence and vague measure convergence. On the two tails their total absolute contribution is <=4C K_C/T. Let T tend to infinity to conclude integral (P_gamma(u)-gamma-u) MA(P_gamma(u))=0.

This reconstructs every finite-tree infimum, descending-limit, compactness, auxiliary support, signed-TV, mixed telescope, local approximation and contact-tail claim in the unchanged paper and its parallel argument. The all-continuous result concerns complete rational affine spaces with REAL references of positive growth. No Bellman iterate or leaf probability was measured, and no limiting domain membership was inferred from a continuity estimate. In a general singular space the latter membership still requires an independent proof.

ordinary_premises_and_complete_reasoning.summary: Primitive determinant and positive subcycle obstruction yield the exact affine-arrangement iff disjoint sector.
ordinary_premises_and_complete_reasoning.detailedSummary: All primitive quotient indices, repeated-factor zero and d! surviving orders give c 2^d d! |det A|. Effective balanced residual and a legal rational transverse flat PCC meet S272 actual-reference jet/roof hypotheses. Separated components give componentwise actual envelopes, synchronized global approximation and raw locality. General singular/literal/abstract cases remain separate.
ordinary_premises_and_complete_reasoning.text:
Verdict for primitive determinants, transverse subcycle obstruction and the finite affine-arrangement iff theorem: PASS under n1-n3. The obstruction requires an actual positive complete saturated plane SUBCYCLE with an explicitly effective BALANCED residual, not merely a plane contained in support.

On a complete saturated d-plane Q of constant weight c, let ell_1,...,ell_d be rational ambient forms and A their restrictions in a saturated basis. A single |ell| divisor is twice its positive evaluation on a primitive complement to its saturated kernel. Indeed the two half-planes have slopes ell and -ell and opposite inward primitive quotient normals, so their raw contributions add. Clear denominators of rational forms by positive rational scaling. For an integer row the Euclidean algorithm makes it (g,0,...,0), g its positive gcd, in a unimodular basis. This simultaneously gives a saturated kernel basis and a primitive complement; no arbitrary unsaturated normal is allowed.

For independent forms, intersect their kernels successively. At each stage the previous lattice is saturated in Q and the next kernel is saturated in it. Extend its basis by a primitive complement. In the resulting nested bases the restriction matrix is triangular; its diagonal entries are exactly the positive primitive evaluations (up to orientation). Their product equals |det A|, including EVERY quotient-normal index. Any ordered product of d distinct |ell_j| therefore gives c 2^d |det A| delta_0. A repeated factor gives zero: use mixed commutation to make its occurrences adjacent, and after its first divisor the factor restricts to zero on the kernel. Expanding (sum |ell_j|)^d leaves d! distinct orders and kills the rest. Thus the RAW atom is c 2^d d! |det A|. This factorial is the count of surviving orders, not an appended operator normalization. Signed and zero cycles are permitted at every stage by n1's conversion. If A is singular, its rational common kernel contains a nonzero line; the germ is constant along that line and the common-lineality raw argument gives zero. These steps prove the general determinant statement independently of the finite checker.

At a rational point v of a finite positive balanced space suppose its tangent cycle C_v contains c[Q], c>0, for a complete rational d-plane, with C_v-c[Q] explicitly effective and balanced. Suppose its support also contains a two-sided rational line L with Q intersect L={0}. Rational linear algebra on Q+L extends a saturated dual basis of Q to rational AMBIENT forms ell_j annihilating L. Set h=sum |ell_j| on the tangent support. Hyperplane cuts give a finite rational refinement, and ambient convexity implies all printed PCC inequalities. H is homogeneous rational PA. Rational small endpoints on both directions of L lie in incident tangent cells; insert v and those rational rays by a legitimate finite rational refinement. Their equal positive weights give a legal flat PCC at rational center v. The center is a common face, not merely an ambient barycenter.

On Q the restriction matrix is the identity, so m0(h;c[Q])=c 2^d d!>0. Raw cycle linearity and positivity on the effective balanced residual give m0(h;C_v)>=that amount. Positivity is justified because h is PC and the residual is balanced; mere positive support would not suffice. S272's actual-reference jet realization applies: gamma is the specified positive-growth REAL PA reference, h is a rational homogeneous PC jet on a finite rational tangent refinement, and v is rational. Its separate rational-reference summands ALL realize the SAME germ C+t+delta h, so convex recombination retains it for the SAME actual gamma. The resulting F is genuine global relative REAL PA PC, has the flat PCC, and has positive raw atom delta^d m0(h). This checks the actual-reference and genuine-domain hypotheses instead of assigning a measure to a formal jet.

Apply the granted roof theorem to that F. Choose a rational ambient polyhedral norm rho and a rational R>0 small enough that the roof neighborhood contains no other raw mass atom and lies in the realized star. The bounded genuine PA obstacle is u=F-gamma+(R-rho(x-v))_+. Its unrestricted envelope is exactly F: the flat boundary relation bounds every competitor at v, radial chords bound rational points under the roof, and shrinking rational simplices in incident faces bound real points (or R230 supplies continuous completion). Outside the roof the obstacle equals F. F itself is a competitor. Only v contributes the nonzero gap to its finite raw measure; its integral is -R delta^d m0(h)<0. All measures and envelopes here are genuinely finite PA; no all-obstacle approximation assumption is needed for this negative witness.

Now let X be a finite union of DISTINCT rational affine d-planes Q_i with positive cycle sum_i c_i[Q_i], saturated tangent lattices and d>=1. At a nonempty intersection rational Gaussian elimination gives a rational intersection center v. For distinct planes through v choose a rational direction a in the second tangent plane outside the first; L=R a intersects the first only at zero and has both signs in the tangent support. The tangent cycle is the sum of precisely those planes through v; subtracting any one positive summand leaves the explicitly effective balanced sum of the others. Hence the obstruction gives a bounded finite-PA negative-contact witness for EVERY actual reference in this sector. For the chosen h the exact origin atom is 2^d d! sum_{i:v in Q_i} c_i|det A_i|; at least one A_i is the identity and singular restrictions contribute zero. Simultaneous all-C_b domain and contact therefore fails whenever planes meet.

For pairwise disjoint affine planes, Q_i-Q_j is a closed affine subspace avoiding zero. Orthogonal projection gives a strictly positive pairwise distance. Finitely many such distances have positive minimum, so each plane is open and closed in X. A convex polyhedral cell is connected and cannot cross these separated components. Any legal PCC has a common center face in its endpoint cells, so ALL its endpoints lie on the same component; this persists on every refinement. Thus printed PC and the actual unrestricted envelope are componentwise. Componentwise competitors patch globally because there are finitely many components and their growth bounds have a finite maximum.

N2 and n3 apply separately to the actual reference and bounded continuous obstacle on each plane. Finitely many decreasing global approximations can be synchronized at the same index, refining their finite rational carriers, with global error the maximum of finitely many component errors. This gives genuine SAME-reference GLOBAL regularization on X. Raw recursion is local and cycle-linear, so finite products and then completed measures are the component sums. Their contact integrals sum to zero. Consequently simultaneous domain membership and exact contact for EVERY bounded continuous obstacle holds IFF the distinct planes are pairwise disjoint. This is the exact scope of the arrangement theorem; it is not only a PA-obstacle assertion.

The lower-dimensional intersections in an intersecting arrangement do not erase its positive complete-plane subcycles. Conversely, no statement is made that every general singular tangent admits such a subcycle. Dimension zero has a separate zero-fold measure and pointwise envelope/contact calculation; it is not proved by the d>=1 determinant obstruction.
